correctness.rationale: The proof gives the exact disjoint even/odd substitution decomposition using synchronization at length 4. Inherited images preserve class membership; closed-end odd factors attach one-to-one; remaining odd factors are isolated by the two circular adjacent-pair matchings (one unique equal closing pair versus at least two equal pairs in the other matching). No probabilistic or finite-extrapolation inference is needed. The closed-end factor doubling and published factor-complexity recurrence yield the dyadic spectrum from the fully enumerated length-four base. The independent standard-library verifier passes all lengths 4..64 for the multiset and all dyadic lengths 4..128 for the complete size distribution and rotation witness.

originality.rationale: The 2014 primary study [1, §5.3] establishes parity synchronization, factor/end-letter recurrences and infinitely many singleton Thue–Morse conjugacy classes, but does not state the exact class-size inflation multiset or complete dyadic size distribution. The 2018 Walnut proof [2, Proposition 1] already establishes only the numeric count \(c(2^k)=2^{k+1}-4\), and the 2021 Lie-complexity paper [3, Example 7.1] counts complete rotation orbits. Those statements do not identify all partial-class sizes. The new claim identifies exactly three two-element classes and all remaining singleton classes and gives a classwise length-doubling recursion at every \(n\ge4\). Targeted searches of published mathematical claims and comparisons against related prior results did not identify such a statement. Historical priority remains qualified; search absence alone is not proof.
residual_risks: A more exhaustive scan of historic cyclic-factor orbit-membership tables, including unindexed sources, could reveal an equivalent size profile.
The older 2014 parity and singleton arguments are close in method; the independent novelty is their exact classwise inflation and dyadic partial-class-size consequence.
No independent formal or outside expert validation has been performed.

value.rationale: The question of how much of each potential circular-rotation orbit actually occurs is a natural strengthening of ordinary cyclic complexity and full-orbit Lie complexity. The theorem determines the entire class-size distribution at infinitely many canonical dyadic lengths, not just the known aggregate count, and gives a reusable exact n-to-2n multiset recursion for all \(n\ge4\). The unique full orbit, three persistent pairs, and linear singleton population reveal structural information not inferable merely from c(n). Historical-priority qualifications are retained.
